PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: char-elijah
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
ELIJAH — IDENTITY INGREDIENTS: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Elijah the Tishbite, the fire-called prophet of Israel, presented as a complete four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet for JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL. He is the same continuous living person locked across every panel: frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body standing figure, pure side profile, and rear-head/costume construction view. One human face exists only on the front of the head; the rear of the skull shows only hair, neck, and mantle folds, never a second face.

Identity and physique: Middle-Eastern Levantine man of the ancient Northern Kingdom of Israel, age appearance approximately fifty-eight to sixty-five years, height about five feet eleven inches, lean wiry wilderness build with ropey forearm and shoulder muscle still intact after ages of waiting, not the young gaunt hollow-cheeked silhouette of John the Baptist and not an elderly snow-white patriarch like Abraham or Moses. Skin is deep sun-leathered olive-bronze, dry and wind-scoured, with fine desert creases at the eyes, bridge of the nose, and corners of the mouth; subsurface warmth returns only where divine gold light kisses the cheekbones and brow. Hands are large, knotted, clean of modern jewelry, with short practical nails, callused palms, and faint old burn freckling on the backs of the fingers as if fire once answered his call. No carried staff, harp, or sword; empty prophetic hands, fingers slightly open as if still feeling the moment the chains fell.

Hair and face: Thick long hair, iron-gray shot through with charcoal-black, wild but fully covering the crown, temples, and rear of the head in every view so the scalp is never bare. The hair falls past the shoulders in heavy weather-beaten locks, coarser and fuller than John's matted younger dark hair, with pale ash-dust still caught in the deeper layers from Hell's chamber. Beard is full, dense, and mid-chest length, the same iron-gray and charcoal mix, shaped by wind rather than barber, split slightly at the chin, not the tear-soaked matted dark beard of John and not the pure winter-white of Adam or Moses. Eyebrows are heavy, dark-gray, and expressive. Eyes are the signature continuity lock: deep amber-brown irises that still hold literal prophetic fire—a banked ember glow in the pupils and a sharp reflective spark along the lower lids—as if Carmel and the chariot of flame never left him. Expression is fierce recognition and coiled intensity: jaw set, nostrils slightly flared, gaze locked forward toward the Harrower with absolute prophetic certainty rather than broken despair. Cheekbones high and hard; mouth firm, lips cracked dry but unbroken; no theatrical smile.

Wardrobe (WARD-ELIJAH — must read differently from John the Baptist's animal skins): Elijah is wrapped in layered animal-skin prophetic garments in the biblical mantle tradition, heavier and more sculptural than John's thinner desert camel-hair tunic. Outer mantle is a dark brown-to-nearly-black coarse goat-hair cloak draped over both shoulders, hanging to mid-calf, with irregular hand-stitched seams, stiff guard hairs catching rim light, and dust-dulled sheen on the grain side. Beneath, a tawny and sand-colored sheepskin wrap bound close to the torso, flesh side inward for insulation, wool side outward in worn patches where the outer mantle parts. A wide rough-tanned leather belt cinches the waist—thick, undecorated, darkened by age and sweat, buckle-less, tied with a rawhide knot. Lower legs remain partly bare between mantle hem and simple hardened leather sole sandals with crossing straps, feet dusty, nails short. No dyed royal cloth, no modern fasteners, no metal ornaments, no logos. Skin and leather read as real animal hide and vegetable-tanned leather under cinematic light, with micro-scuffs, matted hair clumps, and centuries of wear consistent with a wilderness prophet held in Hell's inner chamber until liberation.

Pose and narrative beat: Capture him in the exact screenplay moment when the righteous emerge after the mass chain break—Elijah stepping out of the cold blue torch shadows of Hell's inner fortress chamber into the rising divine gold radiance, animal skins still wrapped about him, fire still in his gaze. Full-body stance is upright, weight slightly forward on the balls of the feet, shoulders squared, chest open, head lifted with prophet authority rather than kneeling penitence. Three-quarter portrait emphasizes the ember eyes, weathered brow, and mantle collar. Side profile locks the nose bridge, beard silhouette, and mantle drape line from crown to mid-calf. Rear view locks complete crown-and-rear hair coverage, the heavy goat-hair mantle back, belt knot, and the fall of layered skins with no face on the back of the head.

Environment and lighting for production reference coherence: Neutral-to-minimal hell-chamber ground plane and soft atmospheric depth rather than a busy set—black stone suggestion, faint residual cold blue torch fill at roughly two thousand Kelvin on one side, and a stronger warm ethereal gold key and rim at roughly fifty-five hundred to sixty-five hundred Kelvin from the divine intrusion, catching hide guard-hairs, iron-gray hair edges, and the wet-look ember spark in the eyes. Subtle volumetric dust motes in the gold beam. Color grade: deep crimson and obsidian shadow pockets, cold blue residual fill, ethereal gold and warm amber on skin and mantle highlights—biblical epic live-action, not illustration, not anime, not CGI cartoon.

Camera and presentation: Photoreal live-action production ingredients sheet, coherent human anatomy and scale across all four panels, clean readable hands, consistent materials, physically plausible subsurface skin and hide fiber. Shallow-to-moderate depth of field appropriate to portrait and full-body reference plates; aspect-friendly framing for cinematic character sheets. Sacred, reverent biblical-epic tone.

Continuity locks repeated for model adherence: Same Elijah identity in every panel—Levantine elder-prophet, iron-gray and charcoal hair with complete crown and rear coverage, full dense matching beard, amber-brown eyes with banked fire still in the gaze, lean wiry build, layered dark goat-hair mantle over tawny sheepskin wrap, wide rawhide-knot leather belt, simple leather sandals, empty hands, one face only on the front of the head. Visually differentiated from John the Baptist by greater age, fuller iron-gray hair and beard, heavier multi-layer animal-skin mantle construction, wiry rather than gaunt dual-prison thinness, and the signature ember-fire gaze motif. No modern objects, no firearms, no eyeglasses, no logos, no readable text, no watermarks, no borders, no captions, no UI chrome, no celebrity likeness. Photorealistic live-action biblical epic production reference only.
